question: I'm writing a JUnit 5 test that needs a scratch folder to unzip some files into. Is it fine to just use JUnit's built-in temp folder injection or File.createTempFile / java.io.tmpdir, and if not, what should I use instead, and how do I get one folder shared across the whole class versus a fresh one per test method?
key_points: Don't use the system temp directory or JUnit 5's @TempDir, since @TempDir also uses the system temp dir. The reasons: leftover data, shared state that breaks other tests, and Jenkins errors when files are created or removed outside the workspace
Use the @XWikiTempDir annotation instead. It creates a unique temporary directory inside Maven's target directory
On a static File field you get one directory per test class. On an instance field you get a new one per test. On a test method parameter you get one just for that test

question: I'm writing a JUnit 5 test for a component that logs an INFO message when it's initialized. That happens once for the whole test class, in the class-level setup, not in each test. Where do I put the log capture and the assertion so the build doesn't fail with an error saying some logged messages were never checked?
key_points: Register the XWiki log-capture JUnit5 extension as a static field (@RegisterExtension private static ...), at a level that includes INFO (e.g. LogLevel.INFO)
Do the assertion in a static @AfterAll method (e.g. assertEquals(expected, logCapture.getMessage(0)))
The extension fails the test (after each test, or after all tests when registered statically) if any captured message was not read via getMessage()/getLogEvent()

question: I'm writing a JUnit5 test for a component whose initialize() method reads some mocked config. One of my test methods needs that mock stubbed differently than the rest, and the stubbing has to happen before initialize() runs. Can I scope that pre-init setup to just that one test method? If so, how, and in what order does it run compared to the shared setup that runs before init?
key_points: Use @BeforeComponent with the test method's name as its value, e.g. @BeforeComponent("myTestName"), on a setup method
That method runs before Initializable#initialize() is called on the component under test
It runs after the unnamed (generic) @BeforeComponent methods
The component manager is rebuilt for each test, so per-test fixtures don't leak between tests (a matching named @AfterComponent also exists)

question: I'm writing a new unit test for one of our XWiki components. Should the test class, the test methods and the setup method that runs before each test be declared with an access modifier, or should I leave it off? Also, how should I name the test methods?
key_points: Do not use the public keyword: JUnit 5 no longer requires it
This applies to the test class, the test methods and the lifecycle methods such as @BeforeEach

Name each test method after the method being tested plus a qualifier (e.g. importWithHeterogeneousEncodings), or after the use case if that doesn't fit, and keep each test to one use case where possible

gold.reference:
= Best practices =

* Name the Test class with the name of the class under test **suffixed with ##Test##**. For example the JUnit test class for ##XWikiMessageTool## should be named ##XWikiMessageToolTest##
* Have each test method test only 1 use case as much as possible.
* Name the test methods with the method to test followed by a qualifier describing the test. For example ##importWithHeterogeneousEncodings()##. In the few cases where it's not applicable, name after the use case being tested.
* Don't use the ##public## keyword since they're not required any more by JUnit5 (not in the Test Class nor in the test methods nor in the lifecycle methods such as ##BeforeEach##).

(Source: https://dev.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Community/Testing/JavaUnitTesting/ , page version 23.1, section "Best practices")
